description:
FOUND s473t6c (#1501 ROUND 10).

t/op/flip.t row 11 is `ok(scalar(15..0))` -- and it passes in perl because in
SCALAR context `..` is the FLIP-FLOP operator, whose constant operands are
implicitly compared against `$.` (the input line number).  With nothing read,
`$.` is undef, so 15 is false, 0 is false, and the flip-flop's own state makes
the expression true in the way the row expects.

PCL evaluates `15..0` as a RANGE even in scalar context, so the row fails.

The other causeless row of the file is NS:Warnings-gated diagnostics (#221)
(it counts two "isn't numeric" warnings).

perlop: "If either operand of scalar `..` is a constant expression, that
operand is considered true if it is equal (`==`) to the current input line
number (the `$.` variable)."  That is the rule to implement; the range half
must not change.
subject: `scalar(15..0)` : a flip-flop whose operands are CONSTANTS compares them against $., so with no input read it is FALSE (op/flip.t row 11)
